questions.stem: Which of the following best describes what statistics is?
options: The process of drawing a random sample from a population
The methods that transform data into useful information for decision makers
A table that lists all possible outcomes of an experiment
The complete count of every item in a population
questions.explain: Statistics = methods that help transform data into useful information for decision makers. 统计学是把数据转化为决策有用信息的方法。

questions.stem: A characteristic of an item or an individual is called a:
questions.explain: A variable is a characteristic of an item or individual (e.g., age of a student). 变量是个体或项目的特征；具体数值才是 data。

questions.stem: The number of cars sold by a dealer each day is:
questions.explain: Countable whole numbers → discrete quantitative. 可数（0,1,2…）→ 离散型定量变量。

questions.stem: The time (in seconds) needed to download a file is:
questions.explain: Time can take any value in an interval → continuous. 时间可在区间内取任意值 → 连续型。

questions.stem: Which of the following is measured on a nominal scale?
options: Order of finish in a race
questions.explain: A student ID only labels; no order or arithmetic. 学号只是标签，不能排序或运算 → 定类尺度。

questions.stem: Temperature measured in degrees Celsius is an example of which measurement scale?
questions.explain: Equal intervals but an arbitrary zero (0°C is not "no temperature") → interval. 间隔相等但零点是人为的 → 定距尺度。

questions.stem: Which measurement scale has a true zero point so that ratios are meaningful?
questions.explain: Only the ratio scale has a true zero (e.g., income, weight). 只有定比尺度有绝对零点，才能说「是两倍」。

questions.stem: A university has 12,000 students. A researcher surveys 300 of them. The 300 students form a:
questions.explain: A subset selected for study is a sample. 被抽取研究的那部分 → 样本；全体 12,000 才是总体。

questions.stem: The average age of all 12,000 students (19.4 years) is a:
questions.explain: A measure describing the whole population is a parameter; one computed from a sample is a statistic. 描述总体的叫参数（parameter），描述样本的叫统计量（statistic）。

questions.stem: Data collected by someone else for a different purpose are called:
questions.explain: Secondary source = the analyst did not collect the data (e.g., census data). 二手资料：分析者不是收集者。

questions.stem: A list of all the items in the population from which a sample is drawn is called a:
questions.explain: The sampling frame is the list used to select the sample. 抽样框 = 抽样的名单；如果名单漏掉某些群体，就会产生覆盖误差。

questions.stem: A researcher divides the city into districts, randomly selects 3 districts, and surveys every household in those 3 districts. This is:
questions.explain: Whole groups (clusters) are selected, then all units inside are studied → cluster sampling. 整群抽样：抽群，群内全查。

questions.stem: An auditor selects every 50th invoice after a random starting point. This is:
questions.explain: A fixed interval (k = 50) after a random start → systematic sampling. 等距（系统）抽样。

questions.stem: The difference between a sample estimate and the true population value that arises simply because a sample is used is called:
questions.explain: Sampling error is the random error inherent in using a sample. 抽样误差是抽样本身带来的随机差异；覆盖/无回答/测量误差都属于非抽样误差。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ethical problem in survey design?
options: Publishing the full questionnaire with the report
Using a random number generator to select respondents
Choosing a sample that over-represents one group so the results favour a sponsor
Reporting the margin of error together with the estimate
questions.explain: Deliberately biased sampling or withholding error information is unethical. 故意让样本偏向某方、或隐瞒误差范围，都属伦理问题。

questions.stem: A table that shows the frequency or percentage of each category of a single categorical variable is a:
questions.explain: Summary table = one categorical variable by category. 汇总表：一个分类变量各类别的频数/百分比。

questions.stem: A table that cross-tabulates two categorical variables is called a:
questions.explain: Contingency table = two categorical variables, rows vs columns. 列联表：两个分类变量交叉汇总。

questions.stem: In a contingency table, the totals shown in the right-hand column and bottom row are called:
questions.explain: Row/column totals are marginal frequencies. 行/列的合计叫边际频数；表内每格是联合频数。

questions.stem: Arranging raw data in order from smallest to largest produces:
questions.explain: An ordered array shows the range and helps spot outliers. 有序数组：排序后能看出范围和异常值。

questions.stem: In a stem-and-leaf display of the values 23, 27 and 31, the stem "2" has leaves:
questions.explain: Stem = leading digit(s), leaf = last digit: 23 → leaf 3, 27 → leaf 7. 茎是前导位，叶是末位。

questions.stem: What is the first step in constructing a frequency distribution?
options: Decide on the number of classes
Count the observations in each class
Sort the data and find the range
questions.explain: First sort the data and compute the range, then choose classes and width. 先排序求极差，再定组数和组宽。

questions.stem: A data set has a range of 46. If you want 6 classes, the class width should be:
questions.explain: Width = range ÷ classes = 46 ÷ 6 = 7.67, always round UP → 8. 组宽 = 极差 ÷ 组数，向上取整。

questions.stem: For the class 20 to less than 30, the class midpoint is:
questions.explain: Midpoint = (lower + upper) ÷ 2 = (20 + 30) ÷ 2 = 25. 组中点 =（下限+上限）÷2。

questions.stem: In a sample of 200 observations, 40 fall in a class. The relative frequency of that class is:
questions.explain: Relative frequency = f ÷ n = 40 ÷ 200 = 0.20 = 20%. 相对频数 = 频数 ÷ 样本量。

questions.stem: A histogram with a long tail extending to the right indicates:
questions.explain: The tail points to the right → positively skewed. 尾巴向右 = 右偏（正偏）。

questions.stem: A Pareto chart orders categories by frequency and adds:
questions.explain: Pareto = descending bars + cumulative % line, used to find the vital few. 帕累托图：降序柱 + 累计百分比折线。

questions.stem: In a Pareto chart, the "vital few" are:
options: The categories with the smallest frequencies
The categories with the largest class width
The categories shown last on the chart
The categories that together account for most of the total
questions.explain: The vital few are the few categories behind most of the problem (often ~80%). 关键少数：占总量大部分的少数类别。

questions.stem: Which chart is most appropriate for showing the proportion of each category of a single qualitative variable?
questions.explain: Pie/bar for categorical; histogram/stem-and-leaf for numerical. 分类变量用饼图/条形图；数值变量用直方图。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a poor practice in graph construction?
options: Starting the vertical axis at a non-zero value to exaggerate differences
Using equal class widths in a histogram
Giving the chart a descriptive title
questions.explain: Truncating the axis exaggerates differences; the vertical axis should start at zero. 纵轴不从 0 开始会夸大差异。

questions.stem: To examine the relationship between two numerical variables you should use a:
questions.explain: Scatter plot for two numerical variables. 两个数值变量的关系用散点图；时间序列用折线图。

questions.stem: A data set contains one extremely large outlier. Which measure of central tendency best represents the typical value?
questions.explain: The median is resistant to outliers; the mean is pulled toward the tail. 中位数不受极端值影响；均值会被拉走。

questions.stem: For a sample of n = 9 ordered values, the median is the:
questions.explain: Median position = (n+1)/2 = 10/2 = 5. 中位数位置 =（n+1）/2。

questions.stem: The mode is:
options: The middle value when data are ordered
The 50th percentile of a grouped distribution
questions.explain: Mode = most frequent value; a data set can have several modes. 众数 = 出现次数最多的值。

questions.stem: The sample variance uses which denominator?
questions.explain: Sample variance divides by n − 1 (degrees of freedom); population variance divides by N. 样本方差分母是 n−1；总体方差分母是 N。

questions.stem: Which measure of dispersion is expressed in the same units as the original data?
questions.explain: Standard deviation is the square root of variance, so it keeps the data units. 标准差与原始数据同单位；方差是平方单位。

questions.stem: The coefficient of variation is most useful when you want to:
options: Compute the range of grouped data
Find the middle value of a data set
Compare variability of data sets with different units or very different means
Detect the shape of a distribution
questions.explain: CV = S ÷ Xbar × 100%, unit-free, so it compares relative variability. 变异系数是无单位的相对离散度，用来跨单位/跨水平比较。

questions.stem: A z-score of +2.5 means the observation is:
questions.explain: Z = (X − Xbar) ÷ S measures distance in standard deviations. Z 分数 = 距离均值多少个标准差。

questions.stem: A z-score with |Z| > 3 is often used to flag:
questions.explain: |Z| > 3 is a common rule of thumb for extreme values. |Z|>3 常用来识别极端值。

questions.stem: For n = 9 ordered values, Q1 is found at position (n+1)/4 = 2.5, which means Q1 is:
options: The average of the 2nd and 3rd values
The average of the 1st and 2nd values
questions.explain: When the position ends in .5, average the two neighbouring values. 位置为 .5 时取相邻两值的平均。

questions.stem: If Q1 = 16 and Q3 = 22, the interquartile range is:
questions.explain: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 22 − 16 = 6; it contains the middle 50% of the data. IQR 覆盖中间 50% 的数据。

questions.stem: In a right-skewed distribution, which statement is normally true?
questions.explain: The mean follows the tail: right skew → mean > median. 右偏时均值被拉向右侧，均值 > 中位数。

questions.stem: According to the empirical rule, about 95% of the values of a bell-shaped distribution lie within:
questions.explain: About 68% within ±1σ, 95% within ±2σ, 99.7% within ±3σ. 经验法则：68 / 95 / 99.7。

questions.stem: For any distribution, Chebyshev’s theorem says the proportion within μ ± 2σ is at least:
questions.explain: 1 − 1/k² with k = 2 gives 1 − 1/4 = 75%. 切比雪夫：至少 1−1/k²。

questions.stem: The mean of grouped data is computed as:
questions.explain: Use class midpoints M weighted by frequencies: Xbar = ΣfM / Σf. 分组数据用组中点加权。

questions.stem: A correlation coefficient of r = −0.85 indicates:
questions.explain: r is between −1 and 1; −0.85 is strong and negative. r 在 −1 到 1 之间；−0.85 是较强的负相关。

questions.stem: The collection of all possible outcomes of an experiment is called the:
questions.explain: Sample space = all possible outcomes. 样本空间 = 全部可能结果。

questions.stem: The probability of any event must be:
questions.explain: 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1 for every event A. 任何事件概率都在 0 与 1 之间。

questions.stem: P(A) + P(A′) = 1 describes the rule of:
questions.explain: A and its complement are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive. 事件与其对立事件互斥且完备。

questions.stem: If A and B are mutually exclusive, which statement is true?
options: A and B always occur together
questions.explain: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together, so their joint probability is 0. 互斥事件不能同时发生，联合概率为 0。

questions.stem: The general addition rule states that P(A or B) equals:
questions.explain: Subtract the overlap once to avoid double counting. 减去一次交集，避免重复计算。

questions.stem: P(A|B) is called the:
options: Joint probability of A and B
Conditional probability of A given B
questions.explain: P(A|B) = P(A and B) ÷ P(B), the probability of A given that B occurred. 条件概率：已知 B 发生时 A 的概率。

questions.stem: Two events A and B are independent if and only if:
questions.explain: Independence means knowing B does not change the probability of A. 独立：知道 B 发生不改变 A 的概率。

questions.stem: If P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5 and A and B are independent, P(A and B) =
questions.explain: For independent events multiply: 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.20. 独立事件用乘法。

questions.stem: Of 200 customers, 120 planned to buy a TV, 60 actually bought one, and 50 both planned and bought. P(bought | planned) =
questions.explain: Condition on the 120 who planned: 50 ÷ 120 = 0.417. 以「计划购买」为条件，除以 120。

questions.stem: Bayes’ theorem is used to:
options: Test whether two events are mutually exclusive
Revise prior probabilities in the light of new information
Compute the mean of a probability distribution
Count the number of possible outcomes
questions.explain: Bayes revises a prior probability to a posterior probability. 贝叶斯用新信息把先验概率更新为后验概率。

questions.stem: A drilling company has P(S) = 0.4 for a successful well. A test gives P(D|S) = 0.6 and P(D|U) = 0.2. P(S|D) is about:
How many outcomes are possible if a fair die is rolled three times?
questions.explain: Counting rule 1: 6 × 6 × 6 = 6³ = 216. 乘法法则：kⁿ。

questions.stem: The number of ways to arrange 3 books out of 5 in order on a shelf is:
questions.explain: Permutations: 5P3 = 5! ÷ (5−3)! = 120 ÷ 2 = 60. 排列：顺序重要。

questions.stem: The number of ways to select 3 books out of 5, ignoring order, is:
questions.explain: Combinations: 5C3 = 5! ÷ (3! 2!) = 10. 组合：顺序不重要。

questions.stem: Selecting 3 students from 5 to form a committee (order does not matter) requires:
questions.explain: Order irrelevant → combination. 顺序无关 → 组合。

questions.stem: A random variable is a variable that:
options: Has a fixed value for each experiment
Assumes numerical values determined by the outcome of an experiment
questions.explain: A random variable maps outcomes to numbers. 随机变量把试验结果映射为数值。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a discrete random variable?
options: The number of defective items in a sample of 100
The time to serve a customer
questions.explain: Counts are discrete; weight, time and temperature are continuous. 计数是离散的。

questions.stem: Which set of probabilities forms a valid probability distribution?
questions.explain: Each probability must lie in [0, 1] and the total must be 1. 每个在 0–1 之间且总和为 1。

questions.stem: X has P(0) = 0.2, P(1) = 0.3, P(2) = 0.5. The expected value E(X) is:
Using the same distribution (E(X) = 1.3), the variance of X is:
Which condition is NOT required for a binomial distribution?
options: A constant probability of success π
A constant number of successes x
A fixed number of trials n
Two mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive outcomes per trial
questions.explain: x varies; what stays constant is n, π and the two-outcome structure. 二项要求：n 固定、两个结果、π 不变、各次独立。

questions.stem: The mean of a binomial distribution is:
questions.explain: Mean = nπ; variance = nπ(1 − π). 二项均值 = nπ。

questions.stem: The variance of a binomial distribution is:
questions.explain: Variance = nπ(1 − π). 二项方差 = nπ(1−π)。

questions.stem: For n = 10 and π = 0.2, P(X = 0) is approximately:
A binomial distribution with π = 0.5 is:
questions.explain: π = 0.5 gives a symmetric shape; skewness depends on π. π=0.5 时对称。

questions.stem: The Poisson distribution is used when you are interested in:
options: The proportion of successes in n trials
The number of events in a given area of opportunity
The sum of two normal variables
The time until the first success
questions.explain: Poisson counts events per unit interval/area; binomial counts successes in n trials. 泊松：单位区间/区域内的事件数。

questions.stem: The Poisson probability formula is:
questions.explain: Poisson: P(x) = e^(−λ)λ^x / x!. 泊松公式。

questions.stem: For a Poisson distribution, the mean and the variance are:
questions.explain: Poisson mean = variance = λ. 泊松均值与方差都等于 λ。

questions.stem: Customers arrive at a mean rate of λ = 2 per hour. P(X = 0) in one hour is about:
questions.explain: P(0) = e⁻² = 0.1353. 没有顾客到达的概率。

questions.stem: The number of calls arriving at a help desk per minute is best modelled by:
questions.explain: Counting arrivals in a time interval → Poisson. 单位时间内到达数 → 泊松。

questions.stem: For a continuous random variable, probability is measured by:
options: The width of the interval only
The area under the curve between two values
The height of the curve at a point
questions.explain: Probability equals area under the density curve; the probability of one exact value is 0. 连续变量用面积表示概率。

questions.stem: The normal distribution is:
options: Symmetric and bell-shaped, with mean = median = mode
Skewed to the right for large σ
questions.explain: Normal is symmetric, bell-shaped, mean = median = mode. 正态分布对称、钟形，三者相等。

questions.stem: The standard normal distribution has:
questions.explain: Standard normal = Z distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. 标准正态：均值 0，标准差 1。

questions.stem: The transformation Z = (X − μ) ÷ σ converts X into:
questions.explain: Z measures how many standard deviations X is from μ. Z 表示距离均值多少个标准差。

questions.stem: X is normal with μ = 100 and σ = 15. P(X < 115) is about:
For the same X ~ N(100, 15), P(X > 115) is about:
questions.explain: Upper tail = 1 − 0.8413 = 0.1587. 上尾 = 1 − 累积概率。

questions.stem: For X ~ N(100, 15), P(85 < X < 115) is about:
questions.explain: Z between −1 and +1 → 0.6826. 两个标准差之内约 68%。

questions.stem: To find the X value corresponding to a known probability, you use:
questions.explain: Rearrange Z = (X − μ)/σ to get X = μ + Zσ. 反解 Z 公式。

questions.stem: For X ~ N(100, 15), the value with 90% of observations below it is about:
The empirical rule says about 99.7% of a normal distribution lies within:
questions.explain: 68.26% / 95.44% / 99.73% within 1 / 2 / 3 standard deviations. 经验法则。

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a property of the normal distribution?
options: The total area under the curve is 1
It is skewed to the right when σ is large
It is symmetric about its mean
Mean, median and mode are equal
questions.explain: Normality is preserved for any σ; changing σ only changes spread. 改变 σ 只改变胖瘦，不会让分布偏斜。

questions.stem: If μ stays the same but σ increases, the normal curve becomes:
questions.explain: Larger σ spreads the curve out and lowers the peak. σ 越大越矮越宽。

questions.stem: On a normal probability plot, points that lie close to a straight line indicate:
questions.explain: A straight-line pattern supports normality; curvature indicates departure. 点接近直线 → 近似正态。

questions.stem: For the standard normal variable Z, P(Z < 0) equals:
questions.explain: The standard normal is symmetric about 0, so half the area lies below. 对称性：一半面积在 0 左侧。

questions.stem: The total area under any normal probability density curve is:
questions.explain: Every probability density integrates to 1. 概率密度曲线下总面积恒为 1。

questions.stem:
Classify each variable below on (a) qualitative or quantitative, (b) if quantitative, discrete or continuous, and (c) the measurement scale (nominal / ordinal / interval / ratio):
i. The brand of a smartphone
ii. The number of text messages sent today
iii. The time spent on social media today (minutes)
iv. A satisfaction rating: poor / fair / good / excellent
v. Body weight in kilograms
questions.model:
i. Brand — qualitative, nominal. 品牌只是标签，不能排序。
ii. Number of messages — quantitative, discrete, ratio (a true zero exists: 0 messages). 计数，有绝对零。
iii. Time in minutes — quantitative, continuous, ratio. 时间可细分，有绝对零。
iv. Satisfaction rating — qualitative, ordinal. 有顺序，但「good」比「fair」好多少无法量化。

questions.stem:
A university wants to estimate the average monthly spending of its 12,000 students. It obtains the class list of all students, randomly selects 20 tutorial groups out of 300, and surveys every student in those groups. Only 68% of the selected students return the questionnaire, and some report their spending by guessing.
(a) Name the sampling method and explain why it is not a simple random sample.
(b) Identify the sampling frame and one coverage problem that could arise.
(c) Name the survey error involved in the low return rate and the one involved in guessing.
questions.model:
(a) Cluster sampling. Groups are randomly selected and every unit inside a selected group is surveyed, so students in the same tutorial share an instructor and timetable and are not selected independently — that is why it is not a simple random sample.
（整群抽样：抽中的群内全查，因此同一群的学生不独立。）

(b) The sampling frame is the list of all 12,000 students (here, the tutorial-group rosters). Coverage problem: students who are on leave, exchange students, or who take no tutorial may not appear on any roster, so they have no chance of being selected → coverage error.
（抽样框 = 全体学生名册；漏掉休学/交换生会造成覆盖误差。）

(c) Low return rate → nonresponse error (those who respond may systematically differ from those who do not). Guessing the amounts → measurement error. Both belong to non-sampling errors.
（无回答误差 + 测量误差，都属于非抽样误差。）

questions.stem:
A manager wants to know whether a new packaging design increases sales.
(a) Distinguish between primary and secondary data and give one example of each for this problem.
(b) List the five steps of the DCOVA framework in order and state what happens in each.
(c) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using secondary data here.
questions.model:
(a) Primary data are collected by the analyst for this specific purpose — e.g., a controlled store test of the new package. Secondary data were collected by someone else for another purpose — e.g., the company’s past sales reports or industry sales statistics.
（一手资料：自己为本次目的收集；二手资料：别人为别的目的收集。）

(b) DCOVA: Define the variables to be studied → Collect the data → Organize the data (tables) → Visualize the data (charts) → Analyze the data (numerical measures, then conclusions).
（定义变量 → 收集 → 整理 → 可视化 → 分析。）

(c) Advantage of secondary data: fast and cheap, may cover a long history. Disadvantage: it was collected for another purpose, so definitions, time periods or coverage may not match, and the quality cannot be controlled.

questions.explain: Human capital = the quality of labour, built through education, training and experience. 人力资本＝教育训练获得的知识与技能。

questions.stem: A point inside the production possibilities frontier is:
questions.explain: Inside the PPF resources are underused, so the point is attainable but inefficient. PPF 内部＝可达到但无效率。

questions.stem: A point outside the production possibilities frontier is:
options: A point of zero opportunity cost
Unattainable with current resources and technology
Attainable if we use resources efficiently
questions.explain: Beyond the frontier cannot be produced with current resources and technology. 超过边界＝现有资源与技术下无法达到。

questions.stem: The PPF bows outward (is concave) mainly because:
options: Opportunity cost increases as more of a good is produced
Resources are identical in all uses
questions.explain: Increasing opportunity cost gives the outward-bowed shape. 机会成本递增导致 PPF 向外凸。

questions.stem: A rational choice compares:
options: Total benefit with total cost only
questions.explain: Choose more if marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost. 理性选择比较边际收益与边际成本。

questions.stem: Economic growth is represented by:
options: An outward shift of the PPF
A downward shift of the PPF
questions.explain: Growth expands production possibilities, shifting the PPF outward. 经济增长＝PPF 外移。

questions.stem: Gains from trade arise mainly because:
options: One party can exploit the other
People specialise in activities where they have a comparative advantage
questions.explain: Specialisation according to comparative advantage raises total output, so both sides gain. 按比较优势专业化，双方都能获益。

questions.stem: Private property rights encourage efficiency because they:
options: Give owners an incentive to use and maintain resources well
questions.explain: Secure property rights create incentives to invest, maintain and trade. 产权带来投资与维护的激励。

questions.stem: Which statement is normative?
options: The unemployment rate rose last year
The government should raise the minimum wage to reduce poverty
A minimum wage above equilibrium creates unemployment
Raising the minimum wage reduces employment by 2%
questions.explain: Normative statements are value judgements ("should"); positive statements are testable facts. 规范陈述含「应该」，是价值判断。

questions.stem: "Other things remaining the same" is the assumption used to:
options: Isolate the effect of one variable at a time
questions.explain: Ceteris paribus lets us isolate one influence at a time. 其他条件不变，用于分离单一变量的影响。

questions.stem: Self-interested choices:
options: Are made by people pursuing their own goals
questions.explain: Self-interest is about pursuing your own goals; it may or may not promote the social interest. 自利≠自私，也未必损害社会利益。

questions.stem: The question "For whom are goods and services produced?" is about:
questions.explain: What = which goods; how = method of production; for whom = distribution. 为谁生产＝分配问题。

questions.stem: A rise in the price of petrol leads many drivers to buy smaller cars. This is best described as:
options: An increase in scarcity of cars
questions.explain: Prices are incentives; people adjust choices as costs change. 价格是激励，人们随成本调整选择。

questions.stem: A market is:
options: A group of firms that agree on output
A government agency that sets prices
A physical building where goods are sold
Any arrangement that brings buyers and sellers together to exchange
questions.explain: A market is any arrangement enabling buyers and sellers to get information and trade. 市场是买卖双方交易的安排，不一定是实体场所。

questions.stem: The law of demand states that, other things remaining the same:
options: As price rises, quantity demanded rises
As income rises, quantity demanded falls
As price rises, quantity demanded falls
questions.explain: Price up → quantity demanded down (inverse relationship). 价格上升，需求量下降。

questions.stem: When the price of a good rises, the substitution effect causes consumers to:
options: Buy less of it and more of substitutes
questions.explain: The good is now relatively more expensive, so consumers substitute other goods. 替代效应：相对变贵，转向替代品。

questions.stem: For a normal good, a fall in price raises the quantity demanded partly because:
options: The good becomes an inferior good
questions.explain: A lower price raises real income, so consumers buy more of a normal good. 价格下降提高实际收入，正常品需求增加。

questions.stem: A demand curve shows:
options: The relationship between income and quantity demanded
The quantity supplied at each price
The relationship between price and quantity demanded, other things constant
The cost of producing each unit
questions.explain: Demand curve: price vs quantity demanded, ceteris paribus. 需求曲线：价格与需求量的关系。

questions.stem: A movement along the demand curve is caused by a change in:
options: The price of the good itself
questions.explain: Only the good’s own price moves you along the curve; other factors shift it. 自身价格→沿曲线移动；其他因素→整条曲线移动。

questions.stem: Which of the following shifts the demand curve for coffee to the right?
options: A fall in the price of coffee
A rise in the price of tea (a substitute)
A fall in consumers’ income (coffee is normal)
A rise in the price of coffee beans
questions.explain: Higher price of a substitute raises demand for coffee. 替代品涨价→本商品需求增加（右移）。

questions.stem: An inferior good is one for which:
options: Quantity supplied falls when price rises
questions.explain: Inferior good: income up → demand down (e.g., instant noodles). 低档品：收入增加，需求减少。

questions.stem: Two goods are substitutes if:
options: A rise in the price of one decreases the demand for the other
A rise in the price of one increases the demand for the other
questions.explain: Substitutes are alternatives; complements are consumed together. 替代品：一涨价，另一个需求上升。

questions.stem: The law of supply states that, other things remaining the same:
options: As price rises, quantity supplied rises
Supply is fixed in the short run
As price rises, quantity supplied falls
questions.explain: Higher price → higher quantity supplied. 价格上升，供给量上升。

questions.stem: Which of the following shifts the supply curve for bread to the left?
options: A fall in the price of flour
An increase in the number of bakeries
A rise in the price of bread
A rise in the wage of bakers
questions.explain: Higher input costs reduce supply (shift left). 投入成本上升→供给减少（左移）。

questions.stem: The minimum supply price is:
options: The price set by the government
The lowest price at which a producer is willing to sell an additional unit
The price at which quantity demanded equals zero
questions.explain: It equals marginal cost — the lowest price for which the unit will be supplied. 最低供给价格＝边际成本。

questions.stem: A market is in equilibrium when:
options: Supply equals demand at every price
questions.explain: Equilibrium: Qd = Qs, so the price has no tendency to change. 均衡：需求量＝供给量。

questions.stem: If the price is above the equilibrium price, there is a:
questions.explain: Above equilibrium Qs > Qd → surplus → sellers cut price. 价格高于均衡→过剩→降价。

questions.stem: If the price is below the equilibrium price, there is a:
questions.explain: Below equilibrium Qd > Qs → shortage → buyers bid the price up. 价格低于均衡→短缺→涨价。

questions.stem: If demand increases and supply does not change, the equilibrium price ___ and the equilibrium quantity ___.
questions.explain: Demand shifts right → price and quantity both rise. 需求右移→价格与数量同时上升。

questions.stem: If supply increases and demand does not change, the equilibrium price ___ and the equilibrium quantity ___.
questions.explain: Supply shifts right → price falls, quantity rises. 供给右移→价格下降、数量上升。

questions.stem: If both demand and supply increase, which outcome is certain?
questions.explain: Quantity definitely rises; the price change is ambiguous. 数量必增，价格方向不确定。

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a resource allocation method discussed in the chapter?
questions.explain: Methods include market price, command, majority rule, contest, first-come, lottery, personal characteristics, force. 配置方式不含「边际成本定价」。

questions.stem: When a market allocates a scarce resource, the people who get it are:
options: Those who are willing and able to pay the price
questions.explain: Market price allocates to those willing and able to pay. 市场按支付意愿与能力分配。

questions.stem: A command system allocates resources by:
options: The order of someone in authority
questions.explain: Command = allocation by order of an authority. 命令制＝按权威者的指令分配。

questions.stem: Majority rule allocates resources:
options: In the way the majority of voters choose
To the first person in line
questions.explain: Majority rule reflects the choice of more than half the voters. 多数票决。

questions.stem: Allocating a prize to the winner of a race is an example of allocation by:
questions.explain: Contest allocates to the winner. 竞赛。

questions.stem: Queuing for concert tickets is allocation by:
questions.explain: First-come, first-served allocates by time of arrival. 先到先得。

questions.stem: Allocating dormitory rooms by random draw is:
questions.explain: Lottery allocates by chance. 抽签。

questions.stem: The value of a good to a buyer is:
options: The average price in the market
The maximum amount the buyer is willing to pay
questions.explain: Value = willingness to pay (marginal benefit). 价值＝支付意愿（边际收益）。

questions.stem: Consumer surplus for one unit is:
questions.explain: CS = WTP − price paid. 消费者剩余＝愿意支付−实际支付。

questions.stem: On a demand and supply diagram, consumer surplus is the area:
options: Below the price and above the supply curve
Above the price and below the demand curve
Between the demand and supply curves
questions.explain: CS is the area under the demand curve above the price. 消费者剩余＝需求曲线下、价格上方的面积。

questions.stem: The supply curve is also the:
questions.explain: Supply = marginal cost (minimum supply price). 供给曲线＝边际成本曲线。

questions.stem: Producer surplus for one unit is:
questions.explain: PS = price − marginal cost. 生产者剩余＝价格−边际成本。

questions.stem: Total surplus equals:
questions.explain: Total surplus = CS + PS, maximised at the efficient quantity. 总剩余＝CS＋PS。

questions.stem: Allocative efficiency occurs when:
options: Quantity is as large as possible
Marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost
questions.explain: Efficient when MSB = MSC. 有效率的条件是边际社会收益＝边际社会成本。

questions.stem: Deadweight loss is:
options: The difference between price and average cost
A loss of surplus caused by inefficient under- or over-production
questions.explain: DWL = lost total surplus from inefficient quantity. 无谓损失＝数量无效率造成的剩余损失。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of market failure?
options: A price equal to marginal cost
questions.explain: Externalities, public goods, monopoly, taxes and price regulation cause market failure. 外部性是市场失灵来源之一。

questions.stem: The "big tradeoff" refers to the conflict between:
questions.explain: Redistributing income to achieve fairness can reduce efficiency. 效率与公平的权衡。

questions.stem: The "fair rules" view of fairness emphasises:
options: Equality of opportunity and private property rights
questions.explain: Fair rules = equality of opportunity, not equality of income. 规则公平＝机会平等，而非结果平等。

questions.stem: A price ceiling is a regulation that makes it illegal to:
options: Charge a price lower than a specified level
Sell a good without a licence
Charge a price higher than a specified level
questions.explain: A price ceiling (cap) sets a legal maximum price. 价格上限＝法定最高价。

questions.stem: A rent ceiling set below the equilibrium rent creates:
questions.explain: Below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied → shortage. 低于均衡→需求>供给→短缺。

questions.stem: When a rent ceiling creates a shortage, one consequence is:
options: A rise in the quantity supplied
A fall in the quantity demanded
questions.explain: Tenants spend more time searching because the price cannot allocate the units. 价格不能出清，找房时间增加。

questions.stem: A black market is:
options: A market where illegal goods are always sold
An illegal market in which the price exceeds the legal price ceiling
questions.explain: Black market = illegal trading at prices above the ceiling. 黑市＝高于上限的非法交易。

questions.stem: An effective rent ceiling is inefficient because it:
options: Decreases the quantity supplied below the efficient level
questions.explain: The quantity traded falls below the efficient level → deadweight loss. 数量低于有效水平→无谓损失。

questions.stem: A price floor is a regulation that makes it illegal to:
options: Charge a price above a specified level
Trade at a price below a specified level
questions.explain: A price floor sets a legal minimum price. 价格下限＝法定最低价。

questions.stem: A minimum wage set above the equilibrium wage creates:
options: No effect on the labour market
questions.explain: Above equilibrium, quantity of labour supplied exceeds quantity demanded → unemployment. 高于均衡→劳动供给>需求→失业。

questions.stem: An effective minimum wage is inefficient because:
options: It decreases employment below the efficient level
It lowers wages for all workers
It increases the quantity of labour employed
questions.explain: Fewer workers are employed than the efficient quantity → lost surplus. 就业量低于有效水平。

questions.stem: Tax incidence refers to:
options: The division of the tax burden between buyers and sellers
The amount of tax revenue collected
The tax rate set by government
questions.explain: Incidence = who bears the burden (who pays more/gets less). 税负归宿＝买卖双方分担。

questions.stem: A tax of $3 per unit on sellers has the same effect on price and quantity as:
questions.explain: A tax on sellers and an equal tax on buyers are equivalent. 对卖方征税与对买方征同额税等价。

questions.stem: With a tax, the price paid by buyers ___ the price received by sellers by the amount of the tax.
questions.explain: The tax drives a wedge: buyer price = seller price + tax. 税楔：买方价＝卖方价＋税。

questions.stem: A tax on a good:
questions.explain: Tax raises the price to buyers and lowers the price to sellers → smaller quantity. 税使交易量减少。

questions.stem: The burden of a tax falls more heavily on:
options: The side of the market that is more elastic
The side of the market that is less elastic
questions.explain: The less elastic side bears more of the tax. 弹性小的一方承担更多税负。

questions.stem: If demand is perfectly inelastic, a tax is paid:
questions.explain: Buyers cannot change quantity, so the price rises by the full tax. 需求完全无弹性→买方承担全部税。

questions.stem: If demand is perfectly elastic, a tax is paid:
questions.explain: Any price rise loses all buyers, so sellers absorb the tax. 需求完全有弹性→卖方承担。

questions.stem: A production quota set below the equilibrium quantity:
options: Raises the price and lowers the quantity
Lowers the price and raises the quantity
questions.explain: Restricting supply raises price and reduces quantity. 配额限制供给→价格上升、数量下降。

questions.stem: A subsidy paid to producers:
options: Lowers the price paid by consumers and raises quantity
Raises the price paid by consumers
questions.explain: A subsidy shifts supply right → lower price, larger quantity (overproduction). 补贴→价格下降、产量增加。

questions.stem: The benefits principle of taxation says that people should pay taxes:
options: According to the benefits they receive from public services
questions.explain: Benefits principle: pay in line with benefits received. 受益原则。

questions.stem: A consumer’s budget line shows:
options: The combinations that give equal utility
The quantities supplied at each price
The combinations of goods the consumer can afford given income and prices
questions.explain: Budget line = affordable combinations. 预算线＝可负担的组合。

questions.stem: Lisa has $40, a movie costs $8 and a case of soda costs $4. The maximum number of movies she can buy is:
questions.explain: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 movies. 全部收入买电影：40/8=5。

questions.stem: With the same $40, $8 per movie and $4 per case of soda, the opportunity cost of one movie is:
questions.explain: One movie costs $8 = 2 cases of soda. 一部电影的机会成本＝2 箱汽水。

questions.stem: If a consumer’s income rises while prices stay constant, the budget line:
options: Shifts outward parallel to the original line
questions.explain: Higher income shifts the budget line outward in parallel. 收入增加→预算线平行外移。

questions.stem: If the price of the good on the x-axis falls, the budget line:
questions.explain: The x-intercept increases; the y-intercept is unchanged → rotation. 横轴商品降价→绕纵轴截距外旋。

questions.stem: Total utility is:
options: The total satisfaction from consuming a given quantity
The extra utility from one more unit
questions.explain: TU = total satisfaction from the quantity consumed. 总效用＝消费某数量的总满足。

questions.stem: If total utility rises from 30 to 42 when consumption increases from 3 to 4 units, marginal utility is:
questions.explain: MU = ΔTU/ΔQ = 12/1 = 12. 边际效用＝总效用增量。

questions.stem: The principle of diminishing marginal utility says that as consumption of a good increases:
questions.explain: Each extra unit adds less satisfaction. 边际效用递减。

questions.stem: A consumer maximises total utility when:
options: Marginal utility is zero for all goods
Spending is equal on all goods
Marginal utility per dollar is equal for all goods
questions.explain: MUx/Px = MUy/Py at the best affordable combination. 每元钱边际效用相等。

questions.stem: If MU of soda per dollar is 10 and MU of movies per dollar is 6, the consumer should:
options: Buy more soda and fewer movies
Buy more movies and less soda
questions.explain: Shift spending toward the good with higher MU per dollar. 增加每元边际效用更高的商品。

questions.stem: Marginal utility theory predicts a downward-sloping demand curve because:
options: A higher price requires a higher marginal utility per dollar to justify buying the good
questions.explain: At a higher price, the good must deliver more MU per dollar to stay in the optimal bundle → less bought. 价格越高，需更高 MU/$ 才值得买，故需求量减少。

questions.stem: When the price of a good falls, the quantity demanded increases because of:
options: The substitution effect and the income effect
questions.explain: Both effects reinforce each other for a normal good. 替代效应＋收入效应。

questions.stem: The paradox of value (water is cheap, diamonds are expensive) is resolved by:
questions.explain: Price reflects marginal utility, not total utility; water has high TU but low MU. 价格由边际效用决定。

questions.stem: Consumer surplus equals:
questions.explain: CS = total value (TU) − amount paid. 消费者剩余＝总价值−总支出。

questions.stem: Bounded rationality means that people:
options: Make choices that are rational within the limits of their information and ability
questions.explain: Bounded rationality: rational but limited by information, time and cognitive ability. 有限理性。

questions.stem: Bounded willpower refers to:
options: The tendency to give in to short-term temptations at the expense of long-term goals
The habit of saving too much
The failure to compare marginal utilities
questions.explain: Bounded willpower: we lack self-control and may regret later. 意志力有限。

questions.stem: Neuroeconomics studies:
options: How the brain makes economic choices
How central banks set interest rates
questions.explain: Neuroeconomics uses brain activity to understand choice. 神经经济学研究决策的脑机制。

questions.stem: The endowment effect is the tendency for people to:
options: Value a good more highly once they own it
questions.explain: Owners demand more to give up a good than they would pay to acquire it. 禀赋效应：拥有后估值更高。

questions.stem: The budget equation PSQS + PMQM = Y states that:
options: Prices are fixed by the government
Income equals the sum of prices
Expenditure on soda plus expenditure on movies equals income
questions.explain: Total spending on the two goods equals income. 两种商品支出之和＝收入。

questions.stem: Real income is:
options: Income expressed as the quantity of goods it can buy
The income earned in the current year
questions.explain: Real income = purchasing power in goods. 实际收入＝能买到的商品数量。

questions.stem: An indifference curve shows:
options: The quantities supplied at each price
The combinations the consumer can afford
Combinations of goods among which the consumer is indifferent
questions.explain: All points on an indifference curve give the same utility. 无差异曲线上效用相同。

questions.stem: A preference map is:
questions.explain: A map of indifference curves, each giving a different utility level. 一组无差异曲线。

questions.stem: A consumer prefers any point on a higher indifference curve because:
options: It lies on the budget line
It has a lower marginal rate of substitution
questions.explain: Higher indifference curves represent higher utility. 越高的无差异曲线效用越大。

questions.stem: Indifference curves cannot cross because:
options: A point could not have two different utility levels
questions.explain: Crossing would violate the assumption that preferences are consistent. 相交会导致同一组合两种效用水平。

questions.stem: The marginal rate of substitution (MRS) measures:
options: The total utility of a bundle
The price ratio of the two goods
The slope of the budget line
The rate at which a consumer will give up one good for another while staying indifferent
questions.explain: MRS = slope of the indifference curve (magnitude): the trade-off keeping utility constant. 边际替代率＝无差异曲线斜率的绝对值。

questions.stem: A diminishing marginal rate of substitution means that indifference curves are:
questions.explain: Diminishing MRS → convex indifference curves. 边际替代率递减→无差异曲线凸向原点。

questions.stem: If two goods are perfect substitutes, the indifference curves are:
questions.explain: Constant MRS → straight-line indifference curves. 完全替代→直线。

questions.stem: If two goods are perfect complements, the indifference curves are:
questions.explain: They are consumed together in fixed proportions → L-shaped. 完全互补→L 形。

questions.stem: The best affordable point is where:
options: The budget line cuts the indifference curve
The indifference curve is tangent to the budget line
questions.explain: Tangency: MRS = relative price and the point is on the budget line. 相切点：MRS＝价格比。

questions.stem: When the price of a good falls, the total change in quantity demanded is the sum of:
options: The substitution effect and the income effect
The price effect and the budget effect
questions.explain: Price effect = substitution effect + income effect. 价格效应＝替代效应＋收入效应。

questions.stem: The substitution effect of a price rise is always:
questions.explain: The direction never varies: higher price → less of that good substituted toward others. 替代效应方向恒为负。

questions.stem: For a normal good, the income effect of a price rise:
questions.explain: Higher price lowers real income → buy less of a normal good. 正常品：价格上升→实际收入下降→需求减少。

questions.stem: For an inferior good, the income effect of a price rise:
options: Is larger in the same direction
questions.explain: Higher price lowers real income, and for an inferior good that raises quantity demanded. 低档品的收入效应与替代效应方向相反。

questions.stem: A Giffen good is one for which:
questions.explain: For a Giffen good the negative income effect dominates the substitution effect. 吉芬商品：收入效应压过替代效应，价格上升需求反而增加。

questions.stem: The demand curve is derived from:
options: The best affordable points as the price changes
questions.explain: Plotting the best affordable quantity at each price gives the demand curve. 由不同价格下的最优消费量推导需求曲线。

questions.stem: If income rises and both goods are normal, the consumer:
options: Moves to a higher indifference curve
Moves along the same indifference curve
questions.explain: Higher income shifts the budget line out → tangency on a higher indifference curve. 收入增加→预算线外移→更高无差异曲线。
